summary: Friedberg argues SpaceX's successful Starship booster catch demonstrates a credible path to $10/kg launch costs, which would make Mars colonization economically feasible and cement SpaceX's dominance in the launch market.
quote: the economics are legit. I mean, this is like a 1,000x reduction in cost. It's incredible.

summary: Friedberg contends Starlink could grow from 4 million subscribers to 100 million or more, potentially becoming one of the largest subscription businesses on Earth as satellite-to-phone expands availability.
quote: Starlink's running at 4 million subs right now. That's like $100 a month, 4 million subs... If we can get satellite to phone and you can get Starlink more broadly available, this could be a 100 million subscriber business.

summary: Chamath argues Expedia is a fragile UI layer on top of licensed third-party data that AI agents will disintermediate, making it a terrible capital allocation at a $30B acquisition price.
quote: I cannot think of a more fragile business model than the UI layer on top of widely available data... a more reasonable assumption is that those things are pretty fragile.

summary: Friedberg sees a financial rationale for Uber acquiring Expedia at ~4x pro forma EBITDA given cost synergies and cross-sell potential, but acknowledges significant strategic AI risk to the business model.
quote: you're kind of paying about $22 billion enterprise value to buy Expedia. So $22 billion of enterprise value, and if you can bump the EBITDA up to $6 billion a year, that's a pretty low multiple.

summary: Sacks argues an Expedia acquisition would destroy value for Uber because cross-selling travel to ride-hailing users fundamentally misunderstands user intent — Uber users want immediate transaction efficiency, not vacation booking.
quote: I'm never going to think to go on my Uber app for that... When I open the Uber app, when I want to hail a taxi, that's why it's like, I rate a guy.

summary: Friedberg says he predicted uranium stocks a year ago and reiterates the bull case: GDP growth drives energy demand that cannot be met without nuclear, making uranium a necessity. He explicitly states his prior year prediction was to buy uranium stocks.
quote: it was also my prediction for the year was to by the uranium stocks predicated on what I think is a really important point, which is as GDP per capita grows, energy consumption per capita grows... there is no way to meet the energy demand without nuclear.
